notes: Yamamoto-first discovery pass under the current durable repository authority. docs/PRIORITIES.md, docs/EDITORIAL.md, docs/DOMAINS.md, radar/inbox/README.md, scripts/validate_events.py, and scripts/merge_inbox.py were reread before publication. Repository-wide duplicate searches were run for each proposed artist/date/venue. Stage 1 admits six performances for specific live-context reasons: BODY&SOUL's documented 52nd-year grand finale; EIC's clarinet/launeddas/electronics-plus-four-percussion instrumental design; Surprise Chef's tightly defined cinematic instrumental language in the immediate window after Frogs In A Pond; Daniel Lanois's sparse three-voice trio configuration; Rishab Rikhiram Sharma's sitar/electronics Sitar For Mental Health program; and Daniel Villarreal's two-night Pan-Latin Solar Myth residency with a named Chicago band. Stage 2 yields A 4 / A+ 1 / S 1 / S+ 0. The BODY&SOUL finale received the required scarcity challenge: the club explicitly identifies September 26 as its grand finale after 52 years and says equipment removal begins the following week before building demolition; A+ would understate genuine-regret scarcity for the last night, while S+ would overstate its broader historical singularity. Japanese local music charges are retained in factual/source notes but not forced into canonical numeric ticket fields because the current validator models ticket currency as USD.

events.subtitle: BODY&SOUL Grand Finale — The Final Groove
events.category: Historic venue farewell / Japanese jazz masters / closing-night performance
events.factual_description: BODY&SOUL presents TOKU with the Tsuyoshi Yamamoto Group on Saturday, September 26, 2026 as the club's documented grand finale. The first set opens at 17:00 and starts at 18:00; the second opens at 20:00 and starts at 21:00. Both official event pages list TOKU on flugelhorn and voice, Tsuyoshi Yamamoto on piano, Toshio Osumi on drums, Hiroshi Kagawa on bass, and Shinobu Ishizaki on alto saxophone. Each set carries a listed music charge of ¥10,000 before tax / ¥11,000 tax included, and reservations are currently closed. BODY&SOUL's August 14 closure notice states that September 26 is the grand finale of its 52nd year, equipment removal begins the following week, and building demolition is scheduled to begin in mid-October.

enrichment.note: Both exact BODY&SOUL set pages verify date, lineup, music charge and set times, and both say reservations are closed. The club's own closure notice verifies the grand-finale and imminent teardown context. No active exact purchase destination or exact Apple Music destination is supplied.

sources.note: Primary first-set page verifies September 26, 17:00 doors, 18:00 start, full lineup, listed music charge and closed reservations.
Primary second-set page verifies September 26, 20:00 doors, 21:00 start, same full lineup, listed music charge and closed reservations.
Primary closure notice identifies September 26 as the 52nd-year grand finale, says equipment removal begins the following week, and building demolition begins in mid-October.

provenance.note: Date, two set times, complete announced lineup, local music charge, reservation status and final-night scarcity were verified from BODY&SOUL's exact event and closure pages. Repository searches for TOKU, Tsuyoshi Yamamoto, BODY&SOUL and September 26 returned no existing matching RADAR record before publication.

en.why_it_matters: The club is the event here as much as the band. After 52 years, BODY&SOUL closes its run with TOKU in front of Yamamoto's Kagawa/Osumi rhythm section, widened by Shinobu Ishizaki on alto, and the room begins to come apart the following week. That turns a strong Japanese-jazz lineup into an actual last night: one final chance to hear this music inside a Tokyo institution before the setting disappears.
en.trip_verdict: If September 26 overlaps with Tokyo, protect the evening and build the Shibuya plan around this finale. Both reservation forms are currently closed, so access should be treated as a real constraint rather than assumed; I would not create a dedicated Japan trip without a legitimate way into the room.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí el club importa tanto como la banda. Después de 52 años, BODY&SOUL cierra su historia con TOKU al frente de la sección Kagawa/Osumi de Yamamoto, ampliada por Shinobu Ishizaki en alto, y la semana siguiente empieza el desmantelamiento del lugar. Eso convierte una alineación fuerte de jazz japonés en una verdadera última noche: la última oportunidad de escuchar esta música dentro de una institución de Tokio antes de que desaparezca el escenario.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 26 de septiembre coincide con Tokio, protegería la noche y armaría el plan de Shibuya alrededor de este cierre. Las reservas de ambos sets ya aparecen cerradas, así que el acceso es una restricción real y no algo que convenga dar por hecho; no organizaría un viaje dedicado a Japón sin una vía legítima para entrar.

priority_review.rationale: Concrete scarcity: BODY&SOUL explicitly identifies September 26 as the grand finale of its 52nd year, with equipment removal starting the following week and building demolition in mid-October. The second editorial challenge asked whether A+ would still capture the recommendation; it would understate the genuine regret of missing the final night in the room. S+ was rejected because this is a historically meaningful venue farewell, not a singular event of broad enough consequence to justify alter-plans treatment.

events.subtitle: Atlantidei Japan Tour in Tokyo
events.category: Sardinian contemporary jazz / percussion ensemble / cultural exchange
events.factual_description: KEYSTONE CLUB TOKYO presents EIC's Atlantidei Japan Tour in Tokyo on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, with doors at 19:00 and the performance at 19:30. The venue lists Zoe Pia on clarinet and electronics with percussionists Mattia Pia, Nicola Ciccarelli, Carlo Alberto Chittolina and Paolo Nocentini, and a general music charge of ¥4,000 plus table charge. Caligola Records describes Atlantidei as the debut of a quintet of four classical percussionists with jazz clarinetist Zoe Pia, who also uses launeddas and live electronics on the recording; the music sits between contemporary classical music, jazz and world traditions.

enrichment.note: The exact KEYSTONE CLUB TOKYO page verifies date, time, lineup, local charge and an integrated reservation form, but no separate stable purchase URL is supplied. Caligola Records verifies the album concept and broader instrumentation. No exact Apple Music destination is supplied.

en.why_it_matters: The instrumental design is the reason to notice it: one reed voice and electronics set against four percussionists, with Pia's Sardinian launeddas language sitting behind a project that treats timbre and pulse as the bridge between contemporary composition, jazz and Mediterranean memory. A Japan-tour stop in a small Roppongi room gives that unusually physical chamber setup a concrete live context.
en.trip_verdict: If Tokyo is already in play on September 16 and the evening is open, catch the Keystone set. It is the kind of exploratory small-room date that can deepen a trip, but I would fit it around stronger one-off anchors rather than reorganize the itinerary around it.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para seguirlo está en el diseño instrumental: una sola voz de aliento y electrónica frente a cuatro percusionistas, con el lenguaje sardo de las launeddas de Pia detrás de un proyecto que usa timbre y pulso como puente entre composición contemporánea, jazz y memoria mediterránea. Una parada de la gira japonesa en un cuarto pequeño de Roppongi le da a esa formación casi camerística y muy física un contexto en vivo concreto.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio ya está en juego el 16 de septiembre y la noche está libre, entraría al set de Keystone. Es de esas fechas exploratorias de cuarto pequeño que pueden enriquecer mucho un viaje, pero la acomodaría alrededor de anclas más raras en vez de reorganizar el itinerario por ella.

events.subtitle: Cinematic instrumental soul in the Frogs In A Pond release window
events.factual_description: The Hamilton Live lists Surprise Chef on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 at 8:00 PM, with tickets listed at $25-$40. The band's own Bandcamp tour listings independently place Surprise Chef at The Hamilton Live on November 11. Their fifth studio album, Frogs In A Pond, is scheduled for release October 23, 2026 on Concord Jazz; Concord describes a quartet of Lachlan Stuckey, Jethro Curtin, Carl Lindeberg and Andrew Congues and a suite built from cinematic soul, jazz-funk and late-1960s/1970s European film-score ideas.

en.why_it_matters: Surprise Chef build groove like a film score rather than a jam-band vehicle: bass, drums, guitar and keys leave space for small motifs to move while soul, jazz-funk and hip-hop's sample vocabulary stay in the frame. The Washington date lands less than three weeks after Frogs In A Pond, a deliberately sequenced suite recorded largely live, giving this local stop a fresh musical object to test onstage.
en.trip_verdict: If the Wednesday is open, catch them locally at The Hamilton and let the small-room groove be the reason. The tour offers other cities and the project is active, so this is a strong convenient Washington night rather than a date to displace a rarer event for.

es.why_it_matters: Surprise Chef construye el groove más como una banda sonora que como un vehículo de jam: bajo, batería, guitarra y teclados dejan aire para mover motivos pequeños mientras siguen presentes el soul, el jazz-funk y el vocabulario de samples del hip-hop. La fecha de Washington cae menos de tres semanas después de Frogs In A Pond, una suite secuenciada deliberadamente y grabada casi toda en vivo, así que el concierto local llega con un objeto musical nuevo para poner a prueba en el escenario.
es.trip_verdict: Si el miércoles está libre, los vería localmente en The Hamilton y dejaría que el groove del cuarto pequeño sea la razón. La gira pasa por otras ciudades y el proyecto está activo, así que es una muy buena noche conveniente en Washington, no una fecha para desplazar algo más raro.

en.why_it_matters: Lanois's studio reputation becomes interesting live when the arrangement gets this bare. Guitar, bass and drums are almost secondary to three voices that learned to lock together in a chapel, which puts his obsession with space, decay, texture and emotional imperfection into a format small enough to hear the choices happen. That makes the trio more than a producer playing songs from a long résumé.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for the local Hamilton date if Lanois's sound-world is in the listening thread. There are other stops on the 2026 tour, so the advantage here is getting this unusually stripped configuration in Washington without corridor travel.

es.why_it_matters: La reputación de Lanois como productor se vuelve especialmente interesante en vivo cuando el arreglo queda así de desnudo. Guitarra, bajo y batería casi pasan a segundo plano frente a tres voces que aprendieron a amarrarse en una capilla, y eso deja expuesta su obsesión con el espacio, la caída del sonido, la textura y la imperfección emocional. El trío termina siendo mucho más que un productor tocando canciones de un currículum enorme.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a la fecha local en The Hamilton si el mundo sonoro de Lanois está en el hilo de escucha. Hay otras paradas en la gira de 2026, así que la ventaja aquí es escuchar esta configuración tan reducida en Washington sin necesidad de viajar por el corredor.

events.factual_description: Ars Nova Workshop presents Panama-born, Chicago-based drummer and DJ Daniel Villarreal for a two-night Solar Myth residency on November 6-7, 2026 at 20:00. Friday is announced as a standing show and Saturday as seated. The named Chicago-based band is Villarreal on drums and percussion, Cole DeGenova on keyboards, Nathan Karagianis on guitar, John Sutton on bass and Danjuma Gaskin on congas, with additional special guests not yet named. Ars Nova describes Villarreal's music as a Pan-Latin blend touching psychedelic rock, cumbia, Afrobeat, boogaloo, free jazz, hip-hop and funk, with post-production used as an instrument. The presenter lists $30 advance / $35 day-of-show.

en.why_it_matters: Villarreal's drums sit at the junction of Panamanian memory and Chicago's improvised-music ecosystem, and this residency gives that idea a working band rather than a stylistic list: congas, bass, guitar and keyboards can move from cumbia and Afrobeat into psych, boogaloo, free jazz and hip-hop without leaving the groove. His habit of treating post-production as another instrument also makes the live translation worth hearing.
en.trip_verdict: If Philadelphia is already workable that weekend, choose the standing Friday or seated Saturday format and build a Solar Myth night around it. Two chances and an active project make this better as a strong trip add-on than as the sole reason for a corridor run.

es.why_it_matters: La batería de Villarreal está justo en el cruce entre memoria panameña y la escena de improvisación de Chicago, y esta residencia le da a esa idea una banda de trabajo en vez de una simple lista de estilos: congas, bajo, guitarra y teclados pueden pasar de cumbia y Afrobeat a psicodelia, boogaloo, free jazz y hip-hop sin soltar el groove. Además, su costumbre de tratar la posproducción como otro instrumento vuelve especialmente interesante escuchar cómo traduce ese lenguaje al vivo.
es.trip_verdict: Si Filadelfia ya resulta viable ese fin de semana, escogería entre el viernes de pie o el sábado sentado y armaría una noche en Solar Myth alrededor del set. Dos oportunidades y un proyecto activo hacen que funcione mejor como una muy buena adición al viaje que como la única razón para bajar por el corredor.
